entries.name: LobeHub Icons
entries.why: Logos for every AI model and provider as SVG and React components. Reach for this when a UI needs OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or Ollama marks instead of a robot emoji.

entries.name: Lucide
entries.why: Consistent outline set of roughly 1,600 icons under MIT. The safe default when a project needs one coherent icon language everywhere.

entries.name: Simple Icons
entries.why: Brand marks for thousands of companies with their official hex colors. Use it for stack badges, footers and integration lists.

entries.name: Tabler Icons
entries.why: Over 5,000 MIT icons drawn on a strict 24px grid, with outline and filled variants of most glyphs.

entries.name: Phosphor Icons
entries.why: One icon family in six weights, from hairline to duotone. Useful when a design needs weight contrast without mixing two sets.

entries.name: Complete UI Essential Pack
entries.why: Game-ready chrome in one download: buttons, bars, frames, cursors and icons across several palettes. Drops straight into a game or a game-styled web app.

entries.name: Kenney
entries.why: Thousands of CC0 game assets covering UI packs, fonts and audio. No attribution required, which makes it the least risky starting point.

entries.name: shadcn/ui
entries.why: Copy-paste React components built on Radix and Tailwind. You own the code after pasting, so restyling never fights a library upgrade.

entries.name: OpenGameArt
entries.why: Community library of sprites, tiles, interface art and audio. Licenses are set per upload, so check each one before shipping.

entries.name: NERV UI
entries.why: Evangelion-flavoured interface kit, all monospace warnings and angular panels. Steal the layout language for anything that should feel operational.

entries.name: Godly
entries.why: Hand-picked site designs sorted by style and industry. The fastest way to find a direction when the brief is still vague.

entries.name: Land-book
entries.why: Landing page gallery you can filter by style, colour and category. Better than scrolling a feed when you need one specific layout.

entries.name: Mobbin
entries.why: Screenshots of shipped mobile and web apps organised by flow. Best for seeing how others handled onboarding, paywalls and empty states.

entries.name: Awwwards
entries.why: Award gallery for ambitious web work. Mine it for motion and interaction ideas rather than layouts you can ship on a deadline.

entries.name: Reff Pixels
entries.why: Pixel tilesets and character sheets drawn with one consistent hand. Browse the whole shop before picking, the packs mix together well.

entries.name: CraftPix
entries.why: Large catalogue of 2D game art with a rotating set of freebies. Free and premium terms differ, so read the license on each pack.

entries.name: itch.io game assets
entries.why: The wider marketplace the specialist shops live inside. Sort by free and by tag when you know exactly what is missing.

entries.name: Lospec Palette List
entries.why: Thousands of curated pixel art palettes with hex values ready to copy. Pick one first and a scene reads as a single piece.

entries.name: OverClocked ReMix
entries.why: Decades of free fan-made game music arrangements. Excellent for reference and for listening while you work; clear the license before shipping a track.

entries.name: Freesound
entries.why: Huge library of user-uploaded effects and field recordings. Filter to Creative Commons Zero to skip attribution bookkeeping entirely.

entries.name: Incompetech
entries.why: Kevin MacLeod's royalty-free catalogue, searchable by mood, tempo and genre. Attribution is required on the free tier.

entries.name: Free Music Archive
entries.why: Curated free music with the license printed on every track, which makes clearing usage quick.

entries.name: Game design and self-publishing resource thread
entries.why: Long-running BoardGameGeek thread collecting the unglamorous side of shipping a game: manufacturing, costs, playtesting and distribution.

entries.name: Laws of UX
entries.why: The usability heuristics people quote in design reviews, each with a plain explanation and the original source.

entries.name: Inclusive Components
entries.why: Heydon Pickering rebuilds common components accessibly and explains every decision. Read one before writing your own tabs or menu.

entries.name: Refactoring UI
entries.why: Design advice aimed at developers, from the people behind Tailwind. Concrete rules about spacing, colour and hierarchy rather than theory.
